question.problem:
Fred picked $10$ watermelons from his vegetable garden. The weight of watermelons he grows is normally distributed with a mean of $11\,\text{kg}$ and a standard deviation of $3\,\text{kg}.$ What is the probability that the total weight of the watermelons Fred picked is greater than $100\,\text{kg}$ and less than $110\,\text{kg}?$ You may assume that the weights of the watermelons are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ | $\,0.8508\,$ | $\,0.8531\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ | $\,0.8729\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the weight of the $i$th watermelon. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(11,{3}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 10.
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denotes the total weight of the $10$ watermelons. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{10},
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =10\cdot 11 \\  & =110, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =10\cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =90.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(110,90).
$$

In order to find $P(100<W<110),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(100<W<110) & =P(\frac{100-110}{\sqrt{90}}<Z<\frac{110-110}{\sqrt{90}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.05<Z<0) \\  & =Φ(0)-Φ(-1.05) \\  & =Φ(0)-(1-Φ(1.05)) \\  & =0.5-(1-Φ(1.05)) \\  & =Φ(1.05)-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.05)≈0.8531.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(100<W<110) & ≈Φ(1.05)-0.5 \\  & ≈0.3531.\end{aligned}
$$
